subject: Capacity forecast & commit term — sizing and discount sensitivity
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jamal Turner <jamal.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial capacity ask — expected Q3 peak and commit window

Hi Jamal / Sara,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To get ahead of procurement questions, can you confirm the following so we can produce an accurate reserved-capacity proposal: 

- Typical concurrent token throughput target during peak (rps / avg seq len)
- Expected 99th pct latency SLO you need (ms)
- How much of traffic you can tolerate on a slightly lower-spec model (cost fallback) vs must always hit top-tier model
- Preferred commit term (12 / 24 / 36 months) and any internal discount thresholds we should be aware of

I'll attach a simple template you can fill that maps expected Q3 peak week to GPU-hour needs. We want to align sizing to your product roadmap to avoid over/under-committing.

Attached: acme_capacity_template.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference runtime
From: Jamal Turner <jamal.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — expected Q3 peak and commit window

Dylan,

Thanks — filled a quick pass on the template and attached. High level:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~420 rps, avg seq len 120 tokens.
- 99th pct latency target: 300ms (hard requirement for real-time features).
- Fallback tolerance: we can accept 20% traffic on a lower-cost variant during non-critical windows, but not during real-time inference for product A.
- Prefer 24-month commit but open to 12mo if economics are compelling.

Two procurement questions for your side:
1) How sensitive is the reserved pricing to GPU spot vs on-demand pricing assumptions? Our finance team wants to understand how much the MSRP needs to move if underlying GPU discounts change.
2) Are there approvals required for discounts beyond a standard band?

Attached: acme_capacity_template_filled.xlsx (xlsx)

—Jamal
Jamal Turner
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme capacity template filled — sizing + pricing sensitivity request

Team — forwarding Acme's filled template. Key asks from procurement: sensitivity to GPU discounts and approval path for deeper discounts. TL;DR from my read: 420 rps peak, 300ms 99p target, want 24-mo commit but will consider 12mo if we can lower price.

Can we run a quick scenario analysis: 24-mo and 12-mo commit tiers, with GPU discount assumptions at -0%, -10%, -20% relative to current procurement forecast. Output should be: effective $/GPU-hour, blended $/token at the estimated workload, and recommended commit discount bands we can offer without losing margin.

Also confirm approval chain — who signs off on >20% off list for Dedicated reservations? Procurement warned that their CFO might push to tie discounts to hardware market movement, so we should prepare language on license to adjust pricing if GPU spot market swings beyond X%.

Can someone take this and return numbers by tomorrow EOD? I'll also line up a quick call with Jamal if needed.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamal Turner <jamal.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme capacity template filled — sizing + pricing sensitivity request

Dylan / team / Jamal,

I ran three scenarios and summarized below (high level). Attached is a short memo + a redline of proposed commercial language.

Scenario assumptions (baseline = our current procurement forecast):
- Baseline GPU cost -> unit price X
- GPU discount scenarios: 0% (baseline), 10% discount on HW costs, 20% discount on HW costs
- Two commit terms evaluated: 12mo and 24mo

Findings (blended $/token at Acme projected profile):
- 12mo commit: baseline $0.00095/token, -10% HW -> $0.00086/token, -20% HW -> $0.00078/token
- 24mo commit: baseline $0.00088/token (roughly 7% better than 12mo), -10% HW -> $0.00080/token, -20% HW -> $0.00073/token

Recommended commercial bands we can present (conservative):
- 12mo: up to 12% off list without exec approval; 12–22% needs EVP sales sign-off; >22% requires CRO approval and finance sign-off.
- 24mo: up to 18% off list without exec approval; 18–28% needs EVP sign-off; >28% requires CRO + CFO sign-off.

Contract language suggestion for GPU-market adjustments: include a clause that allows us to re-open pricing if GPU supplier costs move >25% for a rolling 60-day average, with a 30-day notice and mutual remediation options (credit, pass-through, or term adjustment).

Attachments: proposed_terms_v2.pdf (pdf) — includes the commit tiers and redline.

Jamal — happy to walk through the numbers if you'd like. If Acme is strongly leaning to 24mo, the extra 6–8% in effective price buys material buffer vs GPU market risk.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Approval path + next steps for ACME RSV deal

Per Marissa's recommendation — finance has quick guidance on approvals. For deals with <20% discount off our published Dedicated rates, revenue ops can approve. Between 20%–30% requires EVP Sales sign-off and a finance margin check. Anything >30% requires CFO + CRO sign-off and needs a short margin protection schedule.

I've created the DocuSign envelope for the proposed 24-month term at the 18% off band (we're defaulting to conservative language around GPU-market adjustments as Marissa suggested). Link: docusign_ACME_RSV_47.link.txt (link stub).

Next actions:
1) Dylan — set a 30-min call with Jamal to present the 24mo proposal and explain GPU-market clause.
2) Karthik — prepare a short technical note on fallback model behavior during overflow (how we route 20% traffic to cheaper variants without violating SLO).
3) Marissa — hold for EVP queue; if Jamal asks for >22% push, escalate to me for CFO loop.

I'll route the signed LOA to revenue ops once DocuSign completes.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
